chapter: The rhythm section, family and records
title: Bennie and Bus Moten; Basie's debt to Moten
summary: Jones recalls Bennie Moten sitting at the piano and settling the band, while Basie and Bus Moten were busy elsewhere.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Bus Moten, what does he play?
He played the accordion and piano.
That's right. When Bennie would hear the band all messed up, he says, 'is it all right if I have

my band? And he played one tune. He played the tune and when he set down at the piano and the minute he put his hands on the piano - just like Fats Waller, plump! - the whole thing settled. He played "From Outer Space" and when Bennie Moten sat down that's the only time I heard piano. I didn't hear no piano from Basie and Bus. They was too busy drinking and hanging out with chicks. Bennie said, "You can't do that to me." And Bennie would come left field. He'd sit down and say, "All right, fellows." And when he sat down that band became something else. You've seen it with Mr. Ellington.

Well, Basie was mostly the outcome of this because this thing he followed through, just like you say Freddie Greene followed through with the guitar player, Cliff McTyre. Basie must have followed through from the Motens. style and the format of the movements. JAMES: In spiritual values. H: Certainly when we heard the bands, we heard all of you. It was so synonymous that we just considered it more or less a quartet. They are known for the history, for the record, some records - I remember hearing some of them - of just the Basie rhythm section... Well, we'll put one or two of these one. We've got to have some of these in the record.
